failurePolicy.policy: Stop CI immediately; no deploy and no staging data promotion.
Stop CI immediately; block tracker export and commercial endpoints.
Stop CI immediately; session, inactive user, or membership admin bypass found.
Fail PR until allowed and denied sensitive actions create audit events.
Fail PR until source, staging, commit, rollback, and reconciliation counts agree.
Fail PR until webhook idempotency, invoice state, and seat lock reconcile.
Warn and attach artifact diff when smoke or report output changes unexpectedly.
Warn and attach screenshot diff for visual smoke proof, not a release blocker.

releaseGates.rule: test:auth-tenant, test:redaction, test:migrations, and smoke:staging return zero P0 failures.
Every CI job uploads JUnit, JSON, CSV, HTML, or screenshot proof.
Seeded users, records, commercial facts, imports, audit events, and billing fixtures match manifest.
All denied access paths produce audit events and are exportable for governance review.
No live payment keys, charges, or invoices are allowed in staging tests.
Latest restore proof passes after migrations, seed, import, and smoke.
Management can read one CI summary with owner, command, artifact, result, and blocker.
Any failed command links to backend issue labels, owner, and acceptance criteria.

nonNegotiableRules: Never allow a route to accept company_id from a client request.
Never expose commercial vault fields in Tenders or Projects tracker responses.
Never run billing tests with live payment keys.
Never merge if tenant isolation, redaction, migration rollback, or restore proof fails.
Every denied sensitive action must produce an audit event.
Every CI job must publish a readable artifact.
Every workbook import must reconcile source, staging, accepted, rejected, committed, and rollback counts.
Every seed fixture must be traceable to a test command.
Every release candidate must produce a go/no-go summary.
Every failed command must create or link to a backend issue with owner and acceptance criteria.
handoff: Build the private backend repo with these command names from day one so test vocabulary stays stable.
Start with unit, route, auth-tenant, redaction, migration, import, billing, audit, restore, and smoke commands before adding more product scope.
Attach artifacts to every PR and staging run so management can review evidence without reading raw console output.
Treat this JSON as the first CI contract for the production backend repository.
